The green stripe at row 3 could instead be a face-on header label, so this reading is uncertain. Below it, the green board (rows 7-29, 23 rows) is a clear vertical front face carrying the white lettering. A grey ledge at rows 30-31 closes the base. No side face is drawn. It is not a flat slab because the front face is tall.

The panel has a bevelled frame, a darker inner field and a highlight edge, giving about 4 distinct steps on the green material. The references run about 5. Dark edge pixels are 0% near-neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark green rather than a black sticker line, matching the references. For a thin, simple single-tile sign this is a reasonable fit beside the references. It is slightly sparser than the richer references but not flatter than bus-shelter-a, and a careful artist would accept it next to them.

surfaces.part: header cap strip with green label bar
main green sign panel with 약국 lettering

answer.evidence: The object is a flat standing board drawn face-on. The main body is the green panel in rows 7-29, which carries the lettering and a horizontal divider at row 18. The light header in rows 1-5 has a green label bar at rows 3-4 and is the same width as the panel, 13-15 px. It reads as a front-facing header strip, not a receding horizontal surface. It does not widen and narrow like an ellipse. The grey row 5 and dark row 6 look like a frame edge, and the base at rows 30-31 repeats the same grey-then-dark pattern. No top surface, interior contents or side face is shown, so at most a 1-2 row rim exists. The whole drawing is a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical green signboard with white Korean text, drawn at the same scale as the references. It measures 9 visible tones per full tile, which is above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, and the dark edge pixels carry a tint (0% neutral), so the outline reads as a dark green material tone and not a black sticker line. The shading looks like about 4 steps: a dark green border, a mid green face, a lighter panel edge and the white text. The kiosk and vending references show more distinct tones, tiny details and highlights. The candidate's face is a fairly clean, uniform panel with little grain, speckle or wear, so it looks a bit simpler than the richer references. It is comparable to bus-shelter-a, which is also simple and accepted shipped art, but it still falls short of the kiosk and vending machine in surface variation. It is simple and clean, with no outright flat fills, but at best equal to the lowest reference and slightly thinner than the others. When in doubt, fail.

The main body is the green panel in rows 7-29, which carries the lettering and has a dark outline at row 6 and a mirrored base at rows 30-31. The light header in rows 1-5 has a green label stripe at row 3 and a gray edge row at 5, and it mirrors the bottom frame strip (row 30 has the same gray). styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tall green sign with a dark green border, a lighter green inner panel, and white Korean text '약국'. Measured facts: 9 visible tones per tile, which is above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, and the dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted dark green rather than black. By eye, the body has only about 4 lightness steps (dark border, mid green, light panel, white text, small highlight on the left edge). It has little grain or texture beyond the bevel and the text, and the panel is mostly a smooth fill with no speckle. The references (kiosk, vending machine) show more internal detail such as stripes, windows, buttons and panels, so the sign looks simpler and flatter than them. It is comparable to bus-shelter-a, which is itself a simple form. It is a thin sign, so sparseness alone does not count against it. The outline is correct, but the shading depth and surface texture are somewhat lower than the stronger references, and when in doubt the verdict is fail.
